answer: A prism function hashes the agent's stake, work proof, and graph position into one identity commitment. Each agent must stake and solve a unique proof-of-work tied to a per-epoch comet seed, then register a vertex in a sparse Merkle graph where edges require reciprocal attestations. Creating N sybils costs N stakes plus N proofs plus N reciprocal attestations, so attack cost scales linearly while honest participants pay once. From sa0007's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
